brief: NDX fell ~5% last week, a fourth straight weekly decline, as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted a ~28% drawdown over 22 trading days, one of its largest on record. Earnings took a back seat to risk reduction and recalibration of datacenter capex expectations following the midterm election. Flow signals (record put volumes, elevated ETF volumes, panic readings in vol metrics, sell skew, oversold conditions) arguably set up technical relief as volatility normalizes. Fundamentally, investors are becoming more focused on what is priced into 2028+ AI capex and gigawatt build-out, debating whether too much slowdown is already discounted, even as memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility and 3Q earnings stay strong against a backdrop where AI/Semis are down ~40% from highs since summer. Positioning stress continues: long/short books in semis are hard to manage because the short leg is squeezed when the group is compressed, while S&P staples trade at their richest premium to the index in over a decade, prompting questions about crowded defensive rotation. The coming week brings a lighter earnings slate (AMAT, CSCO, TTWO, IFX) plus CPI and PPI data.
